notes: Identical release installations were copied from pgfuzz to zov; postgres SHA-256 hashes match exactly.
Both installations use OpenSSL, assertions disabled, -O2 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer and durable synchronous remote-flush commits.
All compared variants use the same baseline pgbench and baseline standby binary.
Client and replication TLS are enabled in every measured family; remote standby SQL administration uses loopback through SSH.
Large INSERT payloads are generated by SQL on the primary, rather than transmitted as large client parameters.
Run order rotates; medians are medians of per-run quantiles, rather than pooled transaction quantiles.
CPU guards reject an entire affected phase attempt. Unrelated workloads are never stopped by the benchmark.
The first 19-row local attempt compare-zov-core-tls was excluded after Docker image building coincided with 18.35% unattributed busy CPU.
Original transaction logs, server logs, metadata, state and rejected attempts remain under /home/reshke/pgpg2 on zov.
Cross-AZ primary guard is 10% unattributed busy CPU; shared standby guard is 60%. Actual per-window values remain in results.
The two-host topology also separates CPU and persistent volumes; it is not an experiment changing only network RTT.
CPU guards cannot exclude all storage, network, hypervisor or scheduler interference.
RAM saturation and the 50000 TPS RAM control disable TLS and put data/WAL in tmpfs; they do not model persistent-storage durability.
The 50000 TPS rate was chosen once after observing about 61700 TPS baseline saturation, before examining fixed-rate outcomes.
Warmup is 5s; measurement windows are 20s. Each case has three accepted rotating full-variant rounds with seeds 1000,1001,1002.
A CPU-rejected entire round is retried with its original order and seed. Accepted attempts are selected from state.json, not assumed to be a1.
The new candidate is also measured with its worker disabled (off); this includes the wake-after-unlock code.
The tested hybrid variants explicitly use direct_limit=8; this experiment does not measure the enabled-worker default (sync_rep_waker=on, direct_limit=0).
